solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: The road to ruin?

parts.note: a figurative path heading straight for a crash, read literally as a route on which two vehicles must meet head-on

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a course of action bound to end in conflict or disaster, which is a road to ruin taken figuratively.

clue.text: Venue for the policeman's ball?

parts.note: a policeman's ball is a dance for officers, but the clue pictures the building where officers are based as the place it would be held

explanation.walkthrough: COP SHOP is informal British slang for a police station.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a police station, the natural home ground for a constable and so a joking venue for their dance.

clue.text: Sensational start to London university — and free

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter of London is used

parts.note: to rid is to free, as in rid the house of mice

explanation.surface: A tabloid story about the opening of a free university in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid headlines are sensational ones, shocking and luridly coloured to grab attention.

clue.text: One's trapped in one Asian country or another

indicators.note: something trapped in another thing is enclosed by it, so the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: India is one country of Asia
one's is written out as the letters of one plus S

explanation.surface: A person caught inside one country of Asia or perhaps a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Asian country' looks like the definition, but it belongs to the wordplay naming INDIA; the definition is 'another', meaning a second Asian country.
explanation.definitionFit: Indonesia is a different Asian nation from India, so it is the other country the clue gestures towards.

clue.text: Maintains coming back from analysts is nicer

indicators.note: coming back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone claims that, on returning, they find psychoanalysts more pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' marks the letters as taken from inside 'analysts is nicer'; read backwards they give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To insist on something is to maintain it firmly, as in he maintains he was at home.

clue.text: Siemens engineered retribution!

indicators.note: something engineered is constructed or contrived, so the letters of the company name are reassembled

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the German firm Siemens has engineered some revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: Siemens is a German engineering company, which makes 'engineered' read naturally in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis was the Greek goddess of vengeance, and her name is used for deserved punishment or retribution.

clue.text: Weight if spring starts late

indicators.note: a word that starts late has lost its opening letter, so the synonym of spring is shortened at the front

parts.note: a spring or bounce is an elastic leap or quality

explanation.surface: A weight that changes if spring arrives behind schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: An ounce is a small imperial unit of weight, one sixteenth of a pound.

clue.text: Continual stream after Rome is evacuated

indicators.note: after places the stream's synonym behind the letters from Rome
a word that is evacuated has its contents emptied out, leaving just its first and last letters

parts.note: a current is a flowing stream of water or air

explanation.surface: A constant flow of people pours out once Rome has been emptied of its population.
explanation.definitionFit: Something recurrent keeps coming back again and again, so it is continual.

clue.text: Offer support for the last pony in London

parts.note: the end of something is its last part
a pony is a small horse, and a Cockney Londoner drops the H of horse

explanation.surface: Backing the final horse in a race being run in London.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speech, the working-class dialect of London, famously drops initial H, so 'horse' becomes 'orse.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse a person or idea is to give it your public backing or support.

clue.text: Exhibits spread out across area

indicators.note: one piece lying across another is set within it, so the abbreviation sits inside the jumbled letters
spread out suggests the letters are scattered and laid down in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Things on display are laid out over a wide space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns SPREAD into PRADES, and 'across' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To parade something is to show it off, so parades works as a verb meaning exhibits.

clue.text: Threatened to effect a repair to cover crack

indicators.note: one word made to cover another wraps around it, so the expert goes inside the word for repairing

parts.note: to mend is to carry out a repair
a crack player is an ace, an expert

explanation.surface: Someone was threatened into fixing a crack in a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: To menace someone is to threaten them, so menaced is the past tense matching threatened.

clue.text: People who seek pleasure are remarkably dishonest

indicators.note: remarkably hints at something done in a striking or unusual way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A judgement that pleasure-seekers tend to be strikingly dishonest.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedonism is the pursuit of pleasure as life's chief good, and its followers seek enjoyment above all.

clue.text: Blunder covers bishop in flipping eggs

indicators.note: the flipped eggs cover the churchman, wrapping around his abbreviation
flipping something turns it over, so the word for fish eggs is read backwards

parts.note: roe is the mass of eggs of a fish
RR, Right Reverend, is the title abbreviation used for a bishop

explanation.surface: A cook makes a mistake flipping eggs over a bishop's breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' turns the fish eggs round before they wrap the bishop's letters; 'in' is only a link, and the surface's kitchen scene hides the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A blunder is a careless mistake, the same as an error.

clue.text: Leaders of the masses

parts.note: the masses suggests the general population and its rabble-rousers, but read as church services, Masses, their leaders are clergy

explanation.definitionFit: A priest is the clergyman who leads and celebrates the Catholic Mass.

clue.text: How to treat food with a tired air, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters are one possible version of something else, so they are reordered

explanation.surface: Advice on cooking food with a weary air.
explanation.definitionFit: Food can be irradiated, exposed to radiation, to kill bacteria and lengthen shelf life.

clue.text: The highest quality perfumes, reproduced with no end of grief

indicators.note: reproduced suggests a fresh copy so the letters are rearranged, and with no says one letter of the pool is left out of the result
the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: The finest fragrances, copied without any of the trouble of the original.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reproduced, with no end of grief': rearrange PERFUMES once F, the last letter of grief, is taken out of the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Supreme describes something of the highest rank or quality, as in a supreme achievement.

clue.text: Earth, for example, concerned with energy growth

parts.note: Earth is an example of a planet
re means about or concerning, as in business letters
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A remark that our world is involved with the growth of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A plane tree is a large broad-leaved tree, a living growth from the ground.

clue.text: Broadcast by crude-sounding pirate

indicators.note: sounding means the synonym of crude is heard, not seen, so letters that sound like it are used

parts.note: something crude is coarse or vulgar
to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A pirate is put on the air by a vulgar-voiced crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' places AIR beside the sound of COARSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsair was a privateer or pirate, especially one of the Barbary coast.

clue.text: County and cold part of Italy

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps
Umbria is a region of central Italy

explanation.surface: A link drawn between an English county and a chilly area of Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: CUMBRIA is a county in the far north-west of England, home of the Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: Cumbria is one of the counties of England, so it is a specific example of a county.

clue.text: Mainly gamble on excessive love for Italian food

indicators.note: mainly means most but not all, so the word for gamble loses its final letter

parts.note: to risk money is to gamble it
OTT, over the top, means excessive
love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A wager placed on someone's excessive fondness for Italian cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' simply joins the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian dish of rice cooked slowly in stock.

clue.text: King once in search of a hard worker

parts.note: GR, Georgius Rex, was the royal cipher of the King George monarchs of the past
to be after something is to be seeking it

explanation.surface: An old king went looking for a diligent employee.
explanation.definitionFit: Grafter is British slang for someone who works hard and steadily.

clue.text: Wild parties in touring car? Most serious

indicators.note: in places the parties inside the abbreviation for the car

parts.note: GT, gran turismo, denotes a grand touring car
raves are wild all-night dance parties

explanation.surface: Riotous parties held in a touring car are no laughing matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravest is the superlative of grave, meaning most serious or solemn.

clue.text: Never lost heart on the way up — attempt return

indicators.note: in a down clue, on the way up means the letters are read from bottom to top, so backwards
a word that has lost its heart is missing its middle letter

parts.note: a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: An encouraging note to a climber who never lost heart going up and should try again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost heart' removes V from NEVER to leave NEER, which 'on the way up' turns to REEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Re-entry is a coming back in, the act of returning, as a spacecraft does to the atmosphere.

clue.text: Reflective woman of refinement

indicators.note: reflective means mirrored, so the word reads the same in both directions

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A thoughtful lady of good breeding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflective' looks like an adjective for a thoughtful woman, but it says the word mirrors itself and reads the same backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Madam is a polite form of address for a lady, and also a woman of genteel manners.

clue.text: Domestics help in case of magistrates

indicators.note: in puts the word for help inside the outer letters
the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: aid is help

explanation.surface: Household staff assist in a court case heard by magistrates.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a legal case, but 'case of magistrates' means its outer letters, M and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Maids are household servants, and domestics is an older term for such servants.

clue.text: Old friend's impossible situation

parts.note: stale means old and no longer fresh
mate is British slang for a friend; the apostrophe S gives no letter

explanation.surface: An old pal finds themselves in an impossible position.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess, stalemate is a position where no legal move is possible, and by extension any deadlock.

clue.text: Prepare national boxing stadium

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the two words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: Getting a national boxing stadium ready for a big fight.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a level space surrounded by seats for sport or spectacle, a stadium.

clue.text: Monarchist dispensing with good, practical person

indicators.note: dispensing with means doing without, so the letter for good is removed

parts.note: a regalist is a supporter of royal authority, a monarchist

explanation.surface: A royalist who has abandoned goodness becomes a hard-headed pragmatist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monarchist' looks like ROYALIST, but the word needed is REGALIST, a less common synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist deals with things as they actually are, a practical and unsentimental person.

clue.text: Keen listener sent for replacement

parts.note: the ear is the organ that listens, so it is called a listener

indicators.note: letters sent for replacement are swapped about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An eager listener has been dispatched to fill in for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for replacement' reorders SENT as NEST; the ear is called a listener because it is the organ of hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means sincere and intensely serious, as a keen pupil is.

clue.text: Develop hysteria — a proven cure for addiction

indicators.note: to develop is to work into a new form, so the letters given are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Becoming hysterical is a reliable remedy for dependency.
explanation.definitionFit: Aversion therapy treats addiction by pairing the habit with something unpleasant, so the patient is conditioned to avoid it.
